question:
The following pie chart shows the percentage distribution of the expenditure incurred in manufacturing a power bank. Study the pie chart and answer the question.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8d026c03a961c6d2837406712ca1e0057a0d0d66c68600b7df9e70cb90c5b94a.png] 

If 100 power banks are manufactured and the manufacturing cost on them amounts to ₹50,000, then what should be the selling price of the power banks so that the manufacturer can earn a profit of 50%?
solution:
**Given:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8d026c03a961c6d2837406712ca1e0057a0d0d66c68600b7df9e70cb90c5b94a.png] 

Total number power banks manufactured = 100

Manufacturing cost = ₹ 50,000

Profit = 50%

**Formula used:**

Selling price = ((100+ Profit\%)times Cost price )/(100)

**Calculation: **

Manufacturing cost of each power bank = (50000)/(100) = ₹ 500

Total Cost of one power bank = 500times((100\%)/(30 \%)) = ₹ (5000)/(3)

Selling price of the power banks so that the manufacturer can earn a profit of 50% 

⟹ Selling price = ((100+50)timesfrac{5000)/(3)}{100 }

⟹ Selling price = 15times (500)/(3)

⟹ Selling price = ₹ 2500

So, ₹ 2500 will be selling price of the power banks so that the manufacturer can earn a profit of 50%.

Hence, the correct answer is **option 1)**.
